outcomes: A repository declares in one reviewed file the commands its CI runs, the channels a branch, a tag, or a pull request publishes, and the environments that follow those channels, and the CLI tells it what that means before anything runs
A contributor reads one command line — the blocking commands of that file — and knows it is exactly what gates their merge
A workspace without a release-set provider is told so when it authors distribution or environments, instead of declaring authority nothing can serve
nonGoals: Granting, resolving, or checking any authorization: channels, environments, visibility levels, and approvals are declared here and resolved by the execution plane
Migrating an earlier putnami.ci.json: versions 1 and 2 are not read, and the three repositories that authored them migrated by hand
Owning the runner's own configuration, whose content stays open and is preserved unread

requirements.text: putnami.ci.json declares the ordered commands the runner executes, each blocking unless failOnError is false, and the flags appended to the invocation; the generated agent guidance derives its gate line from the blocking commands.

A rule selects one trigger, branches, tags, or pull requests, and lists the channels a publish advances, and may name one baseline channel it measures against but never advances; a tag publishes by convention unless a tags rule opts out; a protected channel is refused in any rule.
An environment declares the channel it follows, its constraints, its rollout, and the workload rules that override them; explain lists the environments that follow each channel a rule advances.

A rule that publishes a channel may declare how long it is kept — while-open on a pull-request rule whose every published channel is per-pull-request, or a whole number of days — validate refuses a lifetime that could never apply soundly, and explain reports the declared lifetime, or its absence, with the rule it matched.
distribution and envs are refused by validate in a workspace without a release-set provider.

validate and fmt accept and preserve an optional closed review profile independently of CI commands and release-set providers, reject unknown authority fields and invalid bounds, and leave target-revision loading, enrollment, credentials and execution to the review plane.
